title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 125
paragraphs: However, when he had come to Athens from Lacedaemon, Timodemos of Aphidnai, one of Themistocles's opponents but otherwise not among the men of distinction, maddened with envy, attacked him, bringing up his trip to Lacedaemon and saying that it was because of Athens that he had received those marks of honor from the Lacedaemonians, not on his own account. As Timodemos kept on repeating this, Themistocles said: “I tell you how it is: if I had been a native of Belbina, I would never have been honored this way by the Spartans; but neither would you have been, my friend — for all that you are an Athenian.” So far, then, went these matters.
